findings.quote: I found how t changes with x
findings.note: Every route on this question begins by differentiating t with respect to x - including mistakes[2], whose student got dt/dx, v and dv/dx right and only stopped one step early. So the right route names a step it shares with the one wrong route on the menu, and a truthful mistakes[2] student could tap it and be recorded as having gone the right way. The step that actually separates the right solver is multiplying dv/dx by v.
findings.fix: I used v times dv over dx

notes: Re-derived: v = 1 over (2ax+b), dv/dx = minus 2av squared, acceleration = v dv/dx = minus 2av cubed, so option 3 is right. Checked the option-2 entry: with dt/dx = a + 2bx the same working gives minus 2bv cubed, so dropping the sign gives 2bv cubed - the entry is arithmetically sound and calculation is a fair type for it (a derivative slip inside a right route). The option-1 distractor flag is honest: no route mixes a and b. mistakes[2] typed concept is right - treating dv/dx as the acceleration is a wrong belief, not a slip. The right_route as written does obey the brief's step-1 rule literally, which is why this is weak and not wrong.
